messages:
maria: quick q — are we settled on per-route 429 headers and burst behavior for the new /v1/generate contract? need wording for SDK docs

ajay: short answer: yes on the main signals. Retry-After when we want clients to pause, X-RateLimit-* for quota bookkeeping. a couple of edge cases for micro-bursts though.

kevin: can you paste the exact header example we should use in the spec?

maria: example we discussed earlier:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712343600
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:generate:abcd1234
```

ellie: question — do we include Retry-After on "soft-429s" (transient bursts where we want clients to slow but not fully block)?

ajay: for soft-429s we usually won't set Retry-After. we'll return 429 with X-RateLimit-Warning: "burst" and maybe a low X-RateLimit-Remaining. Retry-After is reserved for enforced pauses.

samir: SDK guidance idea: if Retry-After present, obey exactly. If not, backoff with exp jitter starting ~100ms up to ~2s and treat X-RateLimit-Remaining<=0 as immediate stop until reset. Also honor X-RateLimit-Reset if present.

maria: agreed. add doc note: "SDKs should treat X-RateLimit-Remaining <= 0 as a hard stop for that bucket; if X-RateLimit-Reset provided, avoid sending requests for that bucket until after reset." pinging @kevin to add to SDK PR.

kevin: will add. small follow-up: is the bucket header name/format final? infra consumers expect X-RateLimit-Bucket.

ajay: yes final: X-RateLimit-Bucket with format route:<name>:<hash>. we will keep legacy X-Quota-Bucket as a shim for 90 days and log deprecation warnings.

ellie: another: if a route-specific quota is hit but account/global quota is still available, do we prefer returning a route 429 or escalate to account-level 429? how should clients see this?

maria: prefer route-first. return 429 with route-scoped headers. ingress routing will still try fallback pathways (cheaper model, different pool) on our side but we want the client to see the route is limited. clients that want cross-route elastic behavior should call the cheaper endpoint.

ops-bot: deploy queued: throttling-policy v3 -> prod at 2024-05-03 03:00 UTC. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/789 (links in infra channel).

samir: small nit — add X-RateLimit-Scope header so SDK can disambiguate quickly (values: route|account|global).

ajay: good call. we'll include X-RateLimit-Scope. updated example below.

maria: final example to land in the API doc:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Scope: route
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712343600
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:generate:abcd1234
X-RateLimit-Warning: burst
```

kevin: backward-compat plan: accept Retry-After as either delta-seconds or HTTP-date for now. announce in changelog.

ellie: timeline for deprecating X-Quota-* shim?

ajay: 90 days after rollout. we'll surface metrics for any clients still using the old header.

maria: thanks all — I'll update the API contract doc and link the SDK PR. unless anyone objects I'll mark this as accepted and close the spec issue.

kevin: +1
samir: +1
ellie: +1
